title: Design System: Pragati Srivastava — The Hackathon Badge

navy.purpose: Page ground, canvas, text on orange, teal and white, ink button.

navy-2.purpose: Booth tabletops and the help desk band.

navy-3.purpose: Desk skirt, navy banner head, ink button hover.

table-lip.purpose: Front edge of a booth table and the clipboard board.

line.purpose: Hairlines on navy; canonical value is rgba(242, 244, 247, 0.14).

white.purpose: Every printed surface and primary text on navy.

paper-2.purpose: Fold band on the desk tent.

orange.purpose: Primary button, ribbon, access strip, sign tiles, banner heads, stubs, skeleton joints.

orange-ink.purpose: Orange for type and marks on white: link underlines, verdict stamps, hover text.

teal.purpose: Alternate zone colour and on states.

teal-ink.purpose: Teal for type and marks on white; selected pose fill; the disc of a struck stamp.

signal-teal.purpose: Teal for light-emitting surfaces: LEDs, bound log lines, kiosk skeleton bones.

kiosk-black.purpose: Screen bezel, event log, port jacks.

rack-line.purpose: Network switch port border and unlit LED.

shadow-ink.purpose: Every cast shadow, as rgba at 0.25 to 0.5 alpha.

badge-name.purpose: PRAGATI on the badge. Uppercase; scaled by the card unit (0.72 below 900px).

banner-title.purpose: Project names on roll-up banners; clamp(2.1rem, 2.85vw, 2.6rem) from 1240px.

reading.purpose: The recognised gesture on the Hands-on booth.

button.purpose: All buttons; 1.2rem in the large size.

label.purpose: Meters, form fields, small captions. Sentence case.

data.purpose: PR and port numbers, owners, log lines, handle, registration values. 0.6875 to 1.0625rem.

shadows.name: paper
shadows.purpose: Stamp card; sheets, tents and forms use 10-18px offsets.

motion.name: lanyard-physics
motion.value: verlet: gravity 2400px/s², step 1/120, 14 iterations, damping 0.993, 12 segments

motion.name: sign-sway
motion.value: scroll-driven, -5deg to 2.6deg to -1deg to 0, entry 10% to cover 35%
motion.purpose: Zone sign settles on view, where animation-timeline is supported.

motion.name: stamp-press
motion.value: 320ms ease-out from scale 1.5, -14deg, to strike angle -6, 5, -3 or 8deg

motion.name: port-flash
motion.purpose: Teal or orange flash on a port result.

motion.name: loading-pulse
motion.purpose: Kiosk tag dot while the model loads.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: global duration clamp to 0.01ms; physics off; flip is an instant swap

narrative.overview:
The portfolio is a hackathon floor at night. Deep navy is the hall. Everything of value is a printed object placed in that hall: a PVC badge on a woven lanyard, hanging zone signs, a check-in desk, roll-up banners, queue tokens, booth tables, wristbands, a sticker sheet, a registration form and a judge's clipboard. The visitor enters with a badge, reads the hook, and walks lettered zones A to I toward the help desk at the exit.

The system gets its identity from the objects, not from page sections. Each zone has its own event-floor object, and that object carries its real content. The objects share one print language: Archivo at very different widths, navy ink on badge white, and flat fields of lanyard orange and teal. The Hands-on booth extends the same language with a kiosk screen and a paper stamp card on a booth table, where a hand skeleton is the live data and, reduced to one ink, the stamp art.

Density is two-layered. The Visitor pass is the short read for a recruiter. The All-access pass adds engineering detail inside the same objects, with no change of layout. The design rejects the white hero over a card grid and the dark terminal page.
keyCharacteristics: Navy hall ground with bright printed objects placed on it.
Archivo width is the main expressive device: 72% on the badge, 118% on the desk tent.
Orange and teal alternate as zone colours; text on both is always navy.
Soft shadows in one navy-black ink lift objects off the floor.
Physical behaviour: the badge swings and flips, signs sway, stamps press.
One layout, two reading depths: Visitor pass and All-access.

rules.name: The Navy Ink Rule
rules.body: Text on orange or teal is always navy (5.76:1 and 5.32:1). White on orange is 2.60:1, so it never appears as text.

rules.name: The Three Teals Rule
rules.body: A hue has one form per surface. Use orange and teal as fills, the ink forms on white, and signal teal on anything that emits light.

rules.name: The Zone Tone Rule
rules.body: Orange and teal alternate through the zone letters, starting with orange at A. The directory tile and the zone sign tile of a zone always match.

rules.name: The Width Is the Voice Rule
rules.body: Width states what kind of print it is. Use 72–78% for the printed identity, 85–92% for sheets and controls, and 105–118% for venue signage and stamps.

rules.name: The Real Data Rule
rules.body: Overpass Mono is for what a system reports: PR numbers, port numbers, owners, log lines, the GitHub handle and registration values. Use it for no other text.

rules.name: The One Shadow Ink Rule
rules.body: Every cast shadow uses rgba(2, 8, 20) with a soft blur, and it lands on the navy floor or a tabletop. Items that sit on white, the portrait and stickers, use a smaller navy-tinted shadow.

rules.name: The Hand-Placed Rule
rules.body: Objects that a person set down tilt slightly: 0.4–1.5° on tickets, wristbands, tents, forms and the stamp card. Stamps may reach 8°, and stickers ±3°. Fixtures stay level: signs at rest, banners, tables and screens.

dos: Do give each new zone a hanging sign and its own event-floor object, not a generic card.
Do set text on orange and teal in navy.
Do use the ink forms of orange and teal on white, and signal teal on dark screens.
Do give light printed surfaces the navy focus ring through the --focus value.
Do cast every shadow from rgba(2, 8, 20) with a soft blur.
Do end every game at the primary email button with a way to play again.
Do label a kiosk's data source on the screen: sample or live.
Do add engineer detail through All-access inside the existing object, with no layout change.
Do keep the portrait at 200 CSS px or less.
donts: Don't turn the page into a white hero over a card grid, or a dark terminal. The black log is a small device on a booth table.
Don't set white text on orange.
Don't use Overpass Mono for prose, headings or button labels.
Don't use the orange focus ring on a white surface: it is 2.60:1 there.
Don't use orange-ink or teal-ink for text on navy.
Don't use sky or sand outside the sticker sheet.
Don't tilt fixtures, or tilt any object beyond the Hand-Placed Rule.
Don't mirror the kiosk's tag or controls; only the lens flips.
